title: Pushes and Pulls
seo_title: Year 1 Science: Pushes and Pulls Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe pushes and pulls in terms of strength and direction and predict the effect of these forces on objects' motion and shape (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 1 science worksheets on pushes and pulls: strong and gentle forces, direction, changing speed and direction, and changing shape by squashing and stretching. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A push or pull makes things move.
key_sub: A bigger push or pull makes a bigger change. Forces can also change shape.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pushes and pulls are forces.

  • A push moves things away from you.
  • A pull moves things towards you.
  • Forces can change speed, direction and shape.
Example

Opening a door towards you: push or pull?

it comes towards you

Answer: pull

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a bigger push makes things go a shorter way.
  • Thinking only pushes can change shape (pulls stretch things).

faq.a: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can start, stop, speed up, slow down or turn moving things.
Squashing, squeezing and pressing are pushes; stretching is a pull. Both can change an object's shape.
Push toy cars with different strengths, roll balls into walls and stretch rubber bands.
